results.summary_before: SPELL is a hardware implementation of a minimal stack-based programming language created for The Skull CTF. It executes a cryptic program stored in EEPROM, using a stack machine architecture with a shift register for serial output. The design is intended as a security challenge, requiring external hardware to load and run the program. No silicon test report is provided, so its hardware behavior is not confirmed.
results.summary: SPELL is a hardware implementation of a minimal stack-based programming language created for The Skull CTF. It executes a cryptic program stored in volatile program memory, using a stack machine architecture with a shift register for serial access. The design provides 256 bytes of program memory, 32 bytes of stack memory, and 32 bytes of data memory, with 8 bidirectional pins and up to 8 output-only pins. Silicon test reports confirm the design works, with successful communication and demo program execution at 10 MHz and overclocking tests up to 156 MHz.
